### Chap. Xvii. . Teaching What Use. May Be Made Of The Former Vifcoufe Of The

IF one demand of the drtift, of what condition, quality or stature the person quesited, or enquired of is, then observe the Signe of that house whereby he is signified, the Signe wherein the Lord of that house is, and wherein the Moone is, mix one with another, and by the greater testimonies judge; for if the Signe be humane, aierhl,that ascends or defends, and the Lord of that Signe or the l in any Sign of the same triplidty oy nature, you may judge the Body to be handsome, and the conditions of the party to bz foci able, or he very courte ous, 8tc.

If the Quere be concerning a Disease, and r be either on the cusp of the Ascendant, or defending in the sixt, you may judge he hath something in his Disease of the nature of r , but what It is, you must know by the concurrence of the other figniheators.

If a Country manor Citizen hath loft or miifeth any Cat , or any materiall thing in his house,3et him observe in what Signe the Significator of the thing is in ; if in y , and it be"a Beast strayed, or the like, let him see what manner of places that Signe directs unto, and let him repaire thither to search, coniidering the quarter of heaven the Signe signifies : if it be an unmoveable piece of Goods, that without man or woman cannot be removed, then let him look into such parts of his house, or about his house as T signifies.

### Chap. Xviii. Of The Essentiall Dignities Of The Planets

THe & way of judicature in Astrology is, first, by being perfect in the nature of the Planets and Signes.

Secondly, by knowing the strength, fortitude or debility of the Planets,Significators,and a well poyiing of them and their alpe&s and severall mixtures, in your judgment.

Thirdly, by rightly applying the influence of the poiiture of Heaven ere&ed, and the Planets alpe&s to one another at the time of the Question, according to natural! (and not enforced) maximes of Art ; for by how much you endeavour to straine a judgment beyond nature, by to much the more you augment your Errour.

THE Ancients doe put this Question to those concerning the ninth house, and I conceive for no other reason, theft because it must be granted* that all Ships are made for Travel! and Journeys: however, in regard the mod part of the ment concerning its safety or ruine is derived from the Ascendant and his Lord, and the Moon , 1 thought fit to place this ment as belonging to the first house.

Generally, the Signe amending and the Moon are Significators of the Ship, and what Goods are in her, the Lord of the Ascendant of those that faile in her : if in the Question demanded you find all these unfortunate, that is, if a malevolent Planet by position be placed in the Ascendant*/ He having dignities in the eighth: or if you find the Lord of the Ascendant in the eighth, in any ill configuration with the Lord of the eighth* twelfth, fourth or sixth, or the Moon combust, or under the eartfv * you may judge the Ship is* loft, and the nien drowned, (unlesse you find reception betwixt themselves) for then the Ship was casually Shipwrackt, aftd some of the Sea-men did escape : but if you find the preceding Significators all of them free from miffortune, both Men and Goods are all safe $ the more safe if any reception be. But if the Ascendant and the Moon be infortunate* and the Lord of the Ascendant fortunate, the Ship is like to be drowned, but the men will be faved : Some for better know ledge and difcovery of what part of the Ship was like to be freest from danger* have divided the severall parts of the Ship*; and havefigaed to every of the twelve Signes, a part or place

To Libra that part which sometimes is aboye3 and feme times below the Water , or betwixt Wind and Weather.

To Scorpio that part where the Seamen are lodged , or doe their Office* To Sagitarius the Mariners themfelvesm to Capricornus the ends of the Ship, to Aquarius the MaHer or Captaine of the Ship * to Pilces the Oates.

Without doubt the true houre of receiving any Question is then, when the Querent propounds his desire unto the Atfrolo - ger, even that very moment of time, in my opinion, is to be : for let us suppose a Letter is sent or delivered unto me, wherein I am desired to resolve some doubts j perhaps I receive the Letter into my hands at three of clock in any day of the week, but in regard of some occasions, doe not read it untill four or five hours after ; that very hour and minute of hour when I, break it open, and perceive the intention of the t Querent* is the time to which I ought to erect my Figure, and- from thence to draw mine Attrologicall Judgment : This way and man have I pradifed , and found successe aniwerable : And Whereas Bmatm and some others doe give warning that the AHrologian judge not his owne Question, and say.he cannot tejl how to accept of a question from himselfe this I conceive was reason, Because he thought the Artifi ,WQuld be partial! to Ifmfelfe in his judgment : Verily I am of a contrary opinion and have found by many experiments* that at what hour the

When to the ninth, it points out a convenient time to un dertake long Journeys, it9s good to study and to follow Learn ing, and to be familiar with Church-men, to study Chymiftry, for it shewes a mind and fancy inclinable to curiolities, &c.

When to the tenth, the Native is inclinable to be ambitious, or to endeavour Preferment, and to be converfan* with men, Magistrates, Nobles, &c. and he (if capable) attains Preferment, or publifce employment in the Common-wealth ;

It notes a fie time in the Tradesman to follow his employment with industry, for it promiseth him much encrease ; he may navigate or journey by Land or Sea with good safety and re putation, shall be much esteemed*

When to the eleventh, it signifies a cheerful! heart and person, the encrease of the Native's Friends, it imports the yeer to be very prosperous in all worldly affaires, and it invites the Native to beftirre himselfe and husband time well, whereby he may much advance his private fortune; &c.

When to the twelft, the Native will be fickly, yet hardly find out or discover the cause, be in condnuall enmity with ill Neighbours, and none knowes for what £ he will be in danger ofimprifonment or banifhment,or hiding his head, unlesse the twelft house in the Radix was fortunate, it imports an unlucky yeer for dealing in great Cattle, and adviseth the Native to be ware of Horfmanihip, H or fe- races. ### Chap. C L X X.

W Hen cither the Signe culminating in the Radix 9 or wherein then the ® was, shall come to ascend in a From ^fettionall Revolution, the Native is then promised good fortuue by his employments publick, by his Profession or Trade, or by some Office or service he shall performe for some great person ; however, it denotes dominion or foveraignty if he be but a petty Constable..

When to the second house, it’s intended the Native shall then receive the profits of his former yeers employment, and shall have in poffeffion that reward which was but formerly promised him.

When to the third house, the Native may & but an in different condition of life : for in regard it’s the sixt house from the tenth, it intends more ill then good, viz . the losse of Kinred, hatred of malicious Neighbours, or robbery in neying.

There may happily be many more Authors extant who liave written of Astrologie, but no more have as yet come unto my hands ; these 1 mention are all my own ,&c. many of these perhaps have been iince printed at other places : Indeed Ptolomey hath been printed in folio, in quarto, in octavo, in fix teens, and hath been tran flated severall times out of Greckjnto Latin : that lately printed at Leiden I conceive to be the mod £t> it was performed by Ailatius, &c. In a word, feme may blame me that I write in the Englijh tongue yet I trust I have offended no man, sith I write in my owne Language ; and to such as speak as I speak 5 nor doe I know that it is forbid unto man to write in his owne Language, or is any man bound to readorheare

that contenteth him not : If this Book doe generally please, I shall account him good, and think him worthy to live 5 but if he difpleafe, I then beleeve the memory of it shall soon perifti* and my selfe shall count kill: If notwithstanding this, mine Accufers will not be satisfied with this common judgment, let them content themselves with the judgment of the time, which at length difcovereth the privy faults of every thing : which because it is the father of truth, it gives judgment without passion, a*nd accuftometh evermore to pronounce true fentence of

the life or death of Writings. Finis $ Deo gloria. Octob. 1. 1 647?
